blocks.path: Heart valve disease
s: Heart valve disease is where 1 or more of the valves in your heart does not work as it should.
It does not always need treatment, but some people will need medicines or surgery.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: Symptoms of heart valve disease can include:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: shortness of breath

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: feeling tired or weak

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: feeling dizzy

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: heart palpitations, where you suddenly feel your heart beating irregularly or faster than usual

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: swollen ankles and feet

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: chest pain or discomfort

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Symptoms of heart valve disease
s: Some people do not have any symptoms.
Sometimes it's found by chance if a doctor hears an unusual sound (a heart murmur) when they listen to your chest.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you're feeling short of breath regularly

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you feel tired, weak or dizzy when doing normal activities

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have heart palpitations that keep coming back, last longer than a few minutes or are getting worse

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have swollen ankles or feet

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have chest pain that comes and goes

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: These symptoms can be caused by many different conditions.
Having them does not definitely mean you have heart valve disease.
But it's important to get them checked by a GP.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you're struggling to breathe – you're choking, gasping and unable to speak

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have sudden chest pain that spreads to your arms, back, neck or jaw, or lasts more than 15 minutes

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have chest pain with shortness of breath or heart palpitations

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Bring any medicines you take with you.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > How heart valve disease is diagnosed
s: If you have symptoms of heart valve disease a GP will listen to your heart.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > How heart valve disease is diagnosed
s: They may arrange tests or refer you to a heart specialist (cardiologist).

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > How heart valve disease is diagnosed
s: Tests you may have include:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > How heart valve disease is diagnosed
s: an ultrasound scan of your heart (echocardiogram)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > How heart valve disease is diagnosed
s: an X-ray of your chest

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > How heart valve disease is diagnosed
s: an electrocardiogram (ECG), where sensors are put on your chest to check your heart

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: If you have mild heart valve disease and you do not have any symptoms, you may not need treatment.
You'll usually have regular check-ups to see if your condition is getting worse.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: If you have symptoms or have severe heart valve disease, you may need medicines to:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: lower your blood pressure and help protect your heart (ACE inhibitors)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: reduce build-up of fluid in your body and lungs (diuretics)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: slow down your heart rate (such as beta blockers)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: reduce the risk of blood clots (anticoagulants)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: If you have severe heart valve disease you'll usually need surgery to either:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: repair the heart valve, if it's not seriously damaged

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease
s: replace the heart valve with an artificial valve or one made from human or animal tissue, if it cannot be repaired

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease > Find out more about heart valve surgery
s: Heart valve replacement

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Treatments for heart valve disease > Find out more about heart valve surgery
s: British Heart Foundation: heart valve repair surgery

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: Heart valve disease affects people differently.
It's common to have mild heart valve disease that does not cause any issues, but for some people it can lead to serious health problems.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: Your care team will tell you what to expect.
They'll also advise on any changes you need to make.
This can include healthy lifestyle changes and avoiding strenuous exercise.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: Possible complications of heart valve disease include:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: heart failure, where your heart cannot pump blood properly

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: atrial fibrillation, where your heart beats irregularly and faster than normal

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: a stroke

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease
s: endocarditis, a serious condition where your heart becomes infected

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease > Heart valve disease in pregnancy
s: It's important to get advice from a heart specialist if you're pregnant or want to get pregnant.
Pregnancy can make heart valve disease symptoms worse.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Complications of heart valve disease > Heart valve disease in pregnancy
s: You can usually have a safe pregnancy, but you may need extra monitoring and treatment.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Types of heart valve disease
s: Heart valve disease happens when 1 of your heart valves either:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Types of heart valve disease
s: does not open fully (called stenosis)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Types of heart valve disease
s: does not close fully (called prolapse) and may be leaky (called regurgitation)

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Types of heart valve disease
s: This means your heart has to work harder to pump blood around your body.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Types of heart valve disease
s: It can affect any of your 4 heart valves, but it's most common in the aortic or mitral valves, on the left side of your heart.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Types of heart valve disease
s: Less commonly it can affect the tricuspid or pulmonary valves, on the right side of your heart.

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Causes of heart valve disease
s: Heart valve disease can be caused by:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Causes of heart valve disease
s: congenital heart disease, where you're born with the condition

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Causes of heart valve disease
s: changes to your heart as you get older, particularly if you smoke or have high blood pressure or high cholesterol

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Causes of heart valve disease
s: conditions that affect your heart, such as rheumatic fever, cardiomyopathy or endocarditis

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Causes of heart valve disease
s: damage from a heart attack

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Help and support for heart valve disease
s: If you have heart valve disease you can get support from charities such as:

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Help and support for heart valve disease
s: the British Heart Foundation

blocks.path: Heart valve disease > Help and support for heart valve disease
s: Heart Valve Voice
